decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: Job gains have moderated, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low.”

changes.quote: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated.”

changes.quote: In recent months, there has been some further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In recent months, there has been modest further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.”

changes.quote: The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals continue to move into better balance.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals have moved toward better balance over the past year.”

changes.quote: The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.”

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; and Christopher J. Waller.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
Job gains have moderated, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.59% APR costs about $89.96 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.09% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.77% would fall by about $11.96 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 76k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3% over the past year (June 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.58%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.52% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 92%, cut 7%, hike 0%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
